overview.description: Move from hand-pipetting to programmable liquid handlers (Opentrons, Hamilton) and robotic workflows. Automation buys reproducibility, throughput, and a traceable record - the reason modern labs and biofoundries scale a protocol from 8 to 800 samples without the error creeping in.
objectives: write a liquid-handling protocol as code (e.g. Opentrons Python API)
define deck layout, labware, and liquid classes; calibrate offsets
judge what is worth automating vs doing by hand
design for traceability - every step logged and reproducible

steps.description: Move from hand-pipetting to programmable liquid handlers (Opentrons, Hamilton) and robotic workflows. Automation buys reproducibility, throughput, and a traceable record - the reason modern labs and biofoundries scale a protocol from 8 to 800 samples without the error creeping in.
steps.intro: A robot only does exactly what you script - the skill is turning a bench protocol into deterministic, calibrated, error-checked code.

instructions.title: Model the protocol
instructions.description: Break the manual protocol into discrete transfers; identify volumes, sources, destinations, and mixing.

instructions.title: Write it as code
instructions.description: Define labware and the deck map, then script the transfers with correct liquid classes (aspiration/dispense rates for viscous or volatile liquids).

instructions.title: Calibrate & dry-run
instructions.description: Calibrate tip and labware offsets, then dry-run without liquid to catch collisions and mispicks before committing samples.

instructions.title: Run, log, iterate
instructions.description: Execute with run logs for traceability; review errors (tip pickup failures, evaporation) and tighten the protocol.

submission.description: Automate one real protocol (e.g. a serial dilution or PCR setup) as a calibrated, dry-run-tested script, and justify why it was worth automating.
